openingPrayer.title: Steady My Heart
openingPrayer.body: Lord, before I read what this day holds, still my heart in You. The world carries heavy news, but You remain unshaken. Give me eyes to see clearly, a heart that does not grow numb or afraid, and wisdom to respond with compassion, not fear. Remind me that You hold every nation, every sorrow, every headline in Your hands. Let my peace rest in You alone, not in what I read today. Amen.

articles.headline: Canada braces for prolonged trade war as counter-tariffs on US take effect
articles.summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20 billion worth of American goods took effect Tuesday, according to BBC News and NPR, escalating a trade dispute with the United States. NPR reports the standoff could have implications reaching beyond the two countries' bilateral relationship, which BBC describes as the world's largest.

articles.headline: At least two people dead after Russian strikes on Kyiv
articles.summary: BBC News reports that at least two people were killed after Russian drone strikes hit Kyiv early Tuesday. Air raid sirens and explosions were reported across Ukraine's capital as the attack unfolded.

verse.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
verse.reflection: For those waking to news of strikes and loss in Kyiv, and nations wrestling over trade and power, this verse offers a steadying reminder: even amid global unrest, God's presence remains near and unshaken.

articles.headline: Canada braces for prolonged trade war as counter-tariffs on US take effect
articles.summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20 billion of American goods took effect Tuesday, according to BBC News, escalating a trade dispute with the United States. NPR reports the move is a direct response to U.S. tariffs and could have effects reaching beyond the two countries. Separately, BBC News reports President Trump has threatened to block U.S. sales of jets made by Canada's Bombardier amid the rising tensions.

articles.headline: Five killed in Miami plane crash were in two vehicles on ground, investigators say
articles.summary: A Boeing 767-300 overshot the runway at Miami International Airport, resulting in five deaths, according to BBC News. Investigators told NPR the victims were inside two vehicles on the ground when the aircraft struck them. Aviation officials are continuing to investigate the circumstances of the crash.

verse.text: The LORD is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.
verse.reflection: Behind today's headlines are real families grieving sudden loss and communities uncertain about what economic conflict will cost them. This verse reminds us that God's nearness isn't reserved for calm days — He draws close precisely when hearts are heavy.

articles.headline: Canada braces for prolonged trade war as counter-tariffs on US take effect
articles.summary: Canada has implemented counter-tariffs on roughly $20 billion worth of U.S. goods, according to BBC News and NPR, escalating a trade dispute with the United States under President Trump. Both outlets note the standoff threatens to disrupt what has long been one of the world's largest bilateral trading relationships, with NPR adding that the economic effects could extend beyond North America.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by 2 outlets (BBC News and NPR)

articles.headline: The 2026 midterm general election season is upon us. Here's what to watch
articles.summary: NPR reports that the 2026 midterm election season has officially begun, with control of Congress at stake as President Trump faces low approval ratings and Democrats show increased enthusiasm. Related NPR coverage highlights that Republicans are holding an unconventional campaign gathering, described as a 'Trumpapalooza,' in Dallas this week to energize voter turnout ahead of the midterms.
articles.trustNote: Multiple related reports from a single outlet: NPR Topics: Politics

verse.text: Where there is no guidance, a people falls, but in an abundance of counselors there is safety.
verse.reflection: Between trade disputes straining nations and elections stirring division, this proverb points us toward the deeper need for wisdom and humility in leadership. May we pray for those who govern, that they seek counsel over conflict.

articles.headline: Canada braces for prolonged trade war as counter-tariffs on US take effect
articles.summary: According to BBC News, Canada has imposed tariffs on roughly $20 billion worth of American goods in response to U.S. trade measures, escalating tensions between the two countries. NPR reports the dispute could have effects reaching beyond North America, and BBC News adds that President Trump has separately threatened to block sales of Canadian-made Bombardier jets in the U.S. amid the standoff.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by BBC News and NPR across multiple articles

articles.headline: Borrowers expecting mortgage rates to drop have hopes dashed
articles.summary: BBC News reports that major mortgage lenders have raised rates on new deals in recent days, disappointing borrowers who had anticipated a decline. The report notes many homeowners now face difficult decisions about when and how to refinance.

verse.text: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
verse.reflection: Between rising mortgage rates and an uncertain trade war, today's news carries a lot of financial anxiety. This verse doesn't ask us to ignore real concerns, but invites us to face them one day at a time, trusting God with what we cannot control.

articles.headline: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI
articles.summary: OpenAI's chief scientist stated in a public post that society is not adequately prepared for the consequences of advanced artificial intelligence, according to BBC News. The comments came as OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, which the company describes as its most powerful AI product yet.

articles.headline: Nvidia strikes $12.9bn deal to buy AI platform Hugging Face
articles.summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire the AI platform Hugging Face in a deal valued at $12.9bn, BBC News reports. The acquisition would give Nvidia control over a widely used open-source AI platform and its developer community.

verse.text: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him.
verse.reflection: As AI grows more powerful and reshapes industries overnight, even its own creators admit uncertainty about what lies ahead. In seasons like this, wisdom isn't found in more data or bigger deals, but in humbly seeking the God who sees the whole picture we cannot.

articles.headline: Pig kidneys keep patients alive long enough to get human kidneys for the first time
articles.summary: According to NPR, doctors used genetically modified pig kidneys to sustain two patients with kidney failure until human kidney transplants became available — the first time this has been achieved. The report describes it as a milestone for xenotransplantation, a field aiming to ease the shortage of donor organs.

articles.headline: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32
articles.summary: BBC News reports on Oli, whose family says his life was permanently altered after emergency department staff in England failed to provide basic care. The outlet's analysis found this case reflects a growing number of clinical negligence claims being filed against A&E departments in England.

verse.text: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
verse.reflection: Today's stories hold both wonder and sorrow — a scientific breakthrough that buys patients precious time, and a family's grief over care that fell short. In both, we're reminded that healing, whether through medicine or mercy, ultimately flows from a God who tends to every wound, seen and unseen.

articles.headline: 'Her body temperature was 106': How heat is killing Americans in their homes
articles.summary: NPR reports that extreme heat kills thousands of Americans annually, with residents of manufactured housing such as mobile homes and trailers facing especially high risk. The report highlights how inadequate insulation and cooling in these homes can lead to dangerously high body temperatures during heat waves.

articles.headline: Trump signs order to remove endangered species protection for grey wolves
articles.summary: According to BBC News, US President Trump has signed an order removing endangered species protections for grey wolves, a move the administration says will benefit ranchers. Conservationists cited by the BBC warn the decision could undermine ongoing efforts to restore wolf populations.

verse.text: They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun smite them: for he that hath mercy on them shall lead them.
verse.reflection: As we read of neighbors suffering in the heat, this promise reminds us that God's compassion moves toward the vulnerable—and calls us to do the same, whether through prayer, policy, or a simple act of care for someone without relief from the sun.

articles.headline: Seven Vermont clergy arrested while protesting ICE targeting center
articles.summary: Seven clergy members in Vermont were arrested while protesting outside a facility reportedly used by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for targeting operations, according to RNS. Among those arrested was Rev. Rebecca Girrell, a United Methodist pastor, who said she felt called as a faith leader to affirm that human beings should not be treated as targets. The incident highlights ongoing involvement by clergy in immigration policy debates.

articles.headline: Church trial of Anglican Archbishop Steve Wood, accused of sexual misconduct, begins Monday
articles.summary: A church trial began this week for Anglican Archbishop Steve Wood, who faces accusations of sexual misconduct, according to RNS. Julian Dobbs, who has taken over the archbishop's duties during the proceedings, described the period as a difficult and uncomfortable season for the denomination in a statement to church members. The trial marks a significant institutional test for the relatively young Anglican province.

verse.text: He has shown you, O mortal, what is good. And what does the Lord require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.reflection: Today's news touches two different calls to justice — clergy standing for the dignity of the vulnerable, and a church confronting hard questions about its own leadership. Micah reminds us that faithfulness isn't abstract; it's lived out in how we treat others and how honestly we hold ourselves accountable.

articles.headline: McTominay heart procedure 'a complete success'
articles.summary: Napoli have confirmed that Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay's heart procedure was 'a complete success,' according to the club. The club expects him to resume training later this month as he continues his recovery.

articles.headline: Como chiefs giving up seats to older fans for Champions League debut
articles.summary: Como president Mirwan Suwarso and several club directors are giving up their tickets to the club's first-ever Champions League match so that elderly supporters can attend, according to BBC Sport. The gesture marks a significant milestone for the Italian club as it makes its debut on Europe's biggest club stage.

verse.text: Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others.
verse.reflection: Whether it's a club celebrating a player's restored health or directors stepping aside so older fans can share in a historic moment, today's sports stories remind us that true joy often comes from putting others first.

articles.headline: Macklemore says 'Free Palestine' call was not an attack on Jewish people
articles.summary: Rapper Macklemore addressed backlash after using the phrase 'Free Palestine' during a recent performance, according to BBC News. He said the statement was not intended as an attack on Jewish people, following calls from some ticket buyers for him to be removed from his tour. The controversy highlights ongoing tensions around how public figures address the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

articles.headline: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer
articles.summary: BBC News presenter Maryam Moshiri has revealed she has been diagnosed with blood cancer, according to BBC News. She told the broadcaster she chose to share her diagnosis publicly in order to raise awareness about the disease. No further details about her treatment or prognosis were included in the report.

verse.text: Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves receive from God.
verse.reflection: Whether facing public misunderstanding or a private diagnosis, both stories today remind us how much courage it takes to speak openly amid uncertainty. May we extend the same compassion to others that we hope to receive in our own hard seasons.

closingBlessing: Whatever today holds, go into it steady — you've already been reminded who's holding it. — Numbers 6:24-26
